lead: Nine festivals that turn the Comunitat Valenciana into the musical epicentre of the Mediterranean every summer. From urban indie to reggae, from the beach to the CAC, from techno to international rock.

From April to September, the Comunitat Valenciana is one of the world’s benchmark destinations for live music lovers. The combination of Mediterranean climate, beaches, unique venues such as the City of Arts and Sciences and a deeply rooted festival tradition has made the region home to some of the most important festivals in Europe.

The calendar kicks off at Easter with SanSan in Benicàssim and does not stop until September with VisorFest at the Marina Norte in Valencia. In summer, the coast fills with beach festivals — Zevra, Arenal Sound and Medusa in Cullera and Burriana — while the city of Valencia hosts the big urban events at the CAC and the Viveros concerts of the Gran Feria de Julio.

items.title: SanSan Festival
items.body: The only festival on the peninsula held at Easter. Three days of indie and national pop with international guests in the coastal enclave of Benicàssim. With the good weather of the Mediterranean spring as a backdrop, SanSan is one of the most original bets on the festival calendar. In 2026 it will feature Of Monsters and Men as international headliners, alongside names such as Rigoberta Bandini, Love of Lesbian, Guitarricadelaguente and La M.O.D.A.

items.title: Festival de les Arts
items.body: “The festival” of Valencia par excellence. In its eleventh edition, the drained lakes of the Ciutat de les Arts host the big stage on which artists such as Siloé, Belén Aguilera, Carlos Sadness, Two Door Cinema Club, Julieta, La La Love You and Pignoise will parade. Sold out after sold out, the Festival de les Arts has established itself as Valencia’s most relevant urban festival, with a line-up that surpasses the previous one every year and an architectural setting without rival in Europe.
facts: Ciutat de les Arts i les Ciències, Valencia

items.title: BIGSOUND Valencia
items.body: The urban music festival that turns Valencia into a Latin epicentre for two nights. In 2026 David Bisbal headlines a top line-up with Lola Índigo, Rels B, Manuel Turizo, Nathy Peluso, Ana Mena, Rigoberta Bandini and Juan Magán. With venues also in Barakaldo, Torrevieja and Pontevedra, the Valencia edition at the CAC is the most spectacular for its stage and for the atmosphere the crowd creates in one of the most photographed spaces in the world.
facts: Ciutat de les Arts i les Ciències, Valencia

items.title: FIB · Festival Internacional de Benicàssim
items.body: The most internationally famous festival in the Comunitat Valenciana. Each edition the FIB attracts thousands of foreign tourists — especially British — who come to Benicàssim drawn by a line-up that always combines big international names with the Mediterranean sun. In 2026, The Prodigy, Franz Ferdinand and Kaiser Chiefs headline a line-up that includes La La Love You and Biffy Clyro. Attending the FIB is also a chance to practise English: international tourism makes this festival a unique cosmopolitan experience.

items.title: Zevra Festival
items.body: The urban music festival on the largest beach on the Spanish Mediterranean. In Cullera, with the waves as a backdrop and the chance to take a dip between performances, Zevra brings together the best of reggaeton and international urban sound. In 2026 the line-up is top-notch: Nicky Jam, Ozuna, Anuel AA, JC Reyes and Saiko lead a proposal that grows more ambitious every year. The combination of beach + urban music + festive atmosphere makes it one of the most complete festival experiences of the summer.

items.title: Arenal Sound
items.body: One of the most massive and eagerly awaited festivals of the Spanish summer, on the shores of the Mediterranean at Burriana beach. A mix of huge concerts, beach atmosphere, beach bars and a chill-out area for those who want the full experience. In 2026, Myke Towers and Dimitri Vegas headline a very broad line-up with María Becerra, Ana Mena, Nil Moliner, Omar Montes, Delaossa, JC Reyes, Juan Magán and dozens more artists. The key “triangle”: accommodation, transport and pass. The rest takes care of itself.
facts: Playa Arenal, Burriana · 30 Jul–2 Aug · From €69.99 · arenalsound.com

items.title: Medusa Sunbeach Festival
items.body: The most important electronic music festival in Spain and one of the greats of Europe. On the beach at Cullera, over five days and nights in August, Medusa brings together the world’s biggest DJs in techno, house, EDM and electronic music. The 2025 line-up — a reference for 2026 — included Afrojack, Alesso, Charlotte de Witte, Nervo and Fatima Hajji. The experience goes beyond the music: the main stage lit up facing the sea at dawn is one of the most iconic images of the Mediterranean summer.

items.title: Rototom Sunsplash
items.body: The most important reggae festival in Europe has been in Benicàssim for more than 30 years. An experience that goes far beyond music: stalls of sustainable products, a family area, restaurants with international cuisine, workshops and activities that make Rototom a temporary community rather than a conventional festival. Good vibes are the common thread. With a line-up that is always top-notch for the genre — top secret until it is announced — Rototom is an essential date for reggae lovers.

items.title: VisorFest
items.body: Valencia’s closest and most intimate festival, true to its identity as a “festival of concerts” with no overlaps and no front stage. VisorFest bets on an experience of proximity between audience and artists, on the Marina Norte stage with the port of Valencia in the background. In 2026 Ride and The Wannadies are the first confirmations, marking the band’s return after their appearance at the inaugural 2018 edition. A quality alternative for stretching the festival summer into autumn.
facts: Marina Norte, Valencia · 25–26 September · From €49 · visorfest.com

blocks.title: Tips for the Valencian festival season
items: Buy well in advance: Festival de les Arts sells out in days; Arenal Sound and Medusa in weeks
For beach festivals in Cullera and Burriana, book accommodation in the area — nearby hotels fill up months ahead
The FIB and Rototom attract massive international tourism — if you are going with big groups, organise transport and camping beforehand
Festival de les Arts and BIGSOUND at the CAC are the most “urban” — you get there by metro (L3, Alameda stop)
SanSan at Easter is the best plan if you want a festival without the summer crowds
VisorFest in September is ideal for closing the season with an intimate festival without the summer hassle
